newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai mayor calls for 10 pct growth for city.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai mayor calls for 10 pct growth for city.

text.p: Shanghai's mayor Xu Kuangdi on Tuesday said the city's target for 1997 was an economic growth rate of 10 percent and commodity price inflation of around six percent.

In a speech delivered to the opening session of the city's People's Congress, the text of which was released to reporters, Xu said the overall economic development of China's largest city was stable and healthy.
He gave the following targets for Shanghai for 1997:
-- gross domestic product (GDP) growth of 10 percent, against 13 percent for 1996.
-- industrial GDP growth of 15-16 percent, against 11.8 percent for 1996.
-- fixed asset investment growth of 11 percent against 15.5 percent for 1996.
-- export growth of 10 percent versus 9.8 percent in 1996.
-- Actual foreign investment of $4.8 billion, about the same as 1996.
-- Commodity price inflation limited to around six percent, against five percent in 1996.
-- Local government tax revenue growth of 13 percent against 26.9 percent in 1996.
